audits.title: Audit on antipsychotic prescribing in children and young people with a learning disability under the care of mental health services in Surrey
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing (tool based on an RCPsych audit)
audits.setting: CAMHS services, Surrey (children and young people with learning disability)

cycle1.result: 5 prescribed antipsychotics, all with documented reason for starting; for 4 started more than 12 months ago, side effects, EPSE, weight, BP, glycaemic control and lipids not documented; 1 had no review in 6 months; 3 reviews did not consider dose reduction or stopping.

audits.other_findings: One patient transferred to primary care with clear transfer of prescribing responsibility and written guidance.
audits.citation: James T, Zainab A, Mura S, Vallance A, Okusi D. Audit on antipsychotic prescribing in children and young people with a learning disability under the care of mental health services in Surrey. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S71-S71. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.229.

audits.title: Implementation of STOMP (Stopping Over-Medication of People With Learning Disability, Autism or Both With Psychotropic Medications) PLEDGE: A Quality Improvement Project at Bradford District Care Foundation Trust CAMHS Learning Disability Team
audits.standard: NHS England STOMP Pledge and local Trust guidelines for antipsychotic physical health monitoring
audits.setting: CAMHS Learning Disability Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 66 (62%) prescribed medication, all eligible for STOMP review; 64 had a behavioural support plan. Of 66: 35% undergoing reduction plan, 35% reduction not suitable, 30% no review or reduction plan.

audits.other_findings: Antipsychotics were the commonest psychotropics (60%); 20 patients (38%) on more than one psychotropic; about 80% on psychotropics over 12 months. Re-audit in a year planned.
audits.citation: Syed M, Ganguly S. Implementation of STOMP (Stopping Over-Medication of People With Learning Disability, Autism or Both With Psychotropic Medications) PLEDGE: A Quality Improvement Project at Bradford District Care Foundation Trust CAMHS Learning Disability Team. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S114-S114. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.343.

audits.title: Audit of Prescribing Practices & Medication Monitoring on Learning Disability Female Low Secure Unit
audits.standard: Trust and national prescribing and monitoring guidelines
audits.setting: Learning disability female low secure forensic unit

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for indications on drug chart, care plans for combined or high-dose antipsychotics, consent to treatment forms, annual health check and psychotropic blood monitoring; MHA capacity assessment forms 71%; valproate annual risk acknowledgement forms 0%.

audits.intervention: Recommended care plans for all patients on valproate with review dates for risk acknowledgement forms, and consistent filing of results.
audits.other_findings: Investigation results were difficult to locate.
audits.citation: England R, Rashid A. Audit of Prescribing Practices & Medication Monitoring on Learning Disability Female Low Secure Unit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S156-S157. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.419.

audits.title: Retrospective Analysis of a Single Centre Experience of the Pharmacological Management of Patients With Intellectual Disability & Challenging Behaviour Across Three Audit Cycles
audits.standard: NICE and STOMP guidelines for pharmacological management of challenging behaviour in intellectual disability
audits.setting: Intellectual disability team, large acute mental health trust

cycle1.result: Risk assessment 68%; description of target behaviour 74%; metabolic monitoring 0%; documentation of interventions 48%; mental health evaluation 87%, physical health 61%; consent 19%; side-effect discussion 32%; 6-week efficacy review 52%; single drug therapy 19%.

cycle2.result: Risk assessment 100%; description of target behaviour 100%; metabolic monitoring 95%; documentation of interventions 86%; mental health evaluation 60%, physical health 60%; consent 46%; side-effect discussion 50%; 6-week efficacy review 50%; single drug therapy 34%; positive behaviour support plan 75%.

audits.other_findings: Intermediate 2014 cycle (n=17): risk assessment 94%, consent 76%, 6-week review 65%. Outpatient-dependent standards were affected by service changes and COVID-19; pharmacy-led reviews suggested.
audits.citation: Khodabux N, Hamid M, Perry R, Cawley-Nash B, Savvopoulou I, Gumber R, et al.. Retrospective Analysis of a Single Centre Experience of the Pharmacological Management of Patients With Intellectual Disability & Challenging Behaviour Across Three Audit Cycles. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S165-S165. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.437.

audits.title: Audit of Patients Prescribed Psychotropic Medication in the Community Learning Disabilities Psychiatry Services of the Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: NHS England STOMP (Stopping Overmedication of People with a Learning Disability, Autism or Both) recommendations
audits.setting: Four Community Learning Disabilities locality teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Good evidence of capacity, consent, best interests, MDT input and regular review of medication, side effects and response (no figures given); rationale for off-label use could be recorded more clearly.

audits.other_findings: Twenty patients were randomly selected per team, excluding those not on psychotropics. Psychotropics still play a significant role in managing behavioural problems.
audits.citation: Adetoki A. Audit of Patients Prescribed Psychotropic Medication in the Community Learning Disabilities Psychiatry Services of the Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S123-S123. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.336.

audits.title: Audit of Compliance With Stopping the Overprescribing of People With Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) and Intellectual Disability (STOMP) Within the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in Warrington, Mersey Care NHS
audits.standard: RCPsych Position Statement PS05/21 (STOMP) and Mersey Care Consent to Examination and Treatment Policy SD06; 14 compliance standards
audits.setting: Alders Warrington CAMHS, Mersey Care NHS

cycle1.result: Overall STOMP compliance 98% (significant assurance); indication documented for all; 1 (6%) had no behavioural support plan before medication; all had MDT before prescribing, 3-monthly reviews, specialist prescriber and capacity documented.

audits.other_findings: Three criteria were not met. 3 (17%) had medication indicated for behavioural problems.
audits.citation: Kwarkas V, Hanna M. Audit of Compliance With Stopping the Overprescribing of People With Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) and Intellectual Disability (STOMP) Within the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in Warrington, Mersey Care NHS. audits.title: STAMP/STOMP Audit: Psychotropic Medication Prescribing and Physical Health Monitoring, for Children and Young People in the Leeds Community Healthcare (LCH) Learning Disability Clinic
audits.setting: Leeds Community Healthcare Learning Disability Clinic (children and young people)

cycle1.result: Annual health check 70%; drug names and doses 100%; indication 85%; side-effect discussion at initiation 73%; side-effect enquiry at follow-up 77%.

cycle2.result: Annual health check 80%; drug names and doses 100%; indication 93%; side-effect discussion at initiation 38%; side-effect enquiry at follow-up 54%.

audits.other_findings: Criteria were changed in cycle 2 (follow-up definition and age >14 for health checks), which may explain differences. Side-effect discussion was often missing for melatonin or ADHD medication.
audits.citation: Akhetuamhen J, Morris E. STAMP/STOMP Audit: Psychotropic Medication Prescribing and Physical Health Monitoring, for Children and Young People in the Leeds Community Healthcare (LCH) Learning Disability Clinic. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S213-S213. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10540.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Psychiatric Discharge Summaries Complying with STOMP (Stopping Over Medication Of People With a Learning Disability and Autism) from Learning Disability Services
audits.standard: NICE NG11: documented rationale, likely treatment length and written strategy for reviewing and stopping psychotropics shared with non-specialists
audits.setting: Four adult learning disability teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 102 (92.7%); review strategy 44 (40%); timescale for stopping 32 (29%).

audits.intervention: Planned: STOMP awareness, STOMP team involvement, discharge template prompts for review/stop timescale and STOMP pathway GP guidance; re-audit in 6 months.
audits.other_findings: 81 patients were prescribed medication for other mental health diagnoses rather than challenging behaviour.
audits.citation: Fernandes R, Donnelly C, Babu P. Clinical Audit of Psychiatric Discharge Summaries Complying with STOMP (Stopping Over Medication Of People With a Learning Disability and Autism) from Learning Disability Services. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S236-S236. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10589.

audits.title: Audit Review of Psychotropic Medication of the Caerphilly Psychiatry Community Learning Disability Caseload
audits.standard: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on regular review and documentation of indication
audits.setting: Community learning disability psychiatry service, Caerphilly

cycle1.result: 114 (97.4%) on at least one psychotropic; 77 (65.8%) on antipsychotics. Indication: clear mental health diagnosis 23/77 (29.9%), behaviours that challenge 15 (19.5%), no clear indication 39 (50.6%). Antidepressants (44): no documented indication in 8 (18.2%).

audits.other_findings: 47 (61.0%) on antipsychotic doses at or below 25% BNF maximum. Medication increased in 27 (23.1%) and reduced in 23 (19.7%).
audits.citation: Lin M, Swift A, Medhurst D. Audit Review of Psychotropic Medication of the Caerphilly Psychiatry Community Learning Disability Caseload. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S316-S316. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11671.

audits.title: Adherence to STOMP principles in CAMHS learning disability services: a clinical audit of prescribing, monitoring, and multidisciplinary practice
audits.setting: Two CAMHS learning disability services (Hereford and Worcester)

cycle1.result: Hereford (n=20) v Worcester (n=12): rationale documented 90% v 100%; reduce/stop plan 10% v 17%; MDT at initiation 30% v 67%; ongoing MDT review 0% v 0%; review ≤6 months 100% v 100%; monitoring complete 11/14 (79%) v 5/6 (83%); capacity/best interests 60% v 100%.

audits.other_findings: Planned actions include a mandatory medication review field in the MDT proforma, scheduled MDT follow-ups and standardised monitoring systems.
audits.citation: Kece B, Powell K. Adherence to STOMP principles in CAMHS learning disability services: a clinical audit of prescribing, monitoring, and multidisciplinary practice. European Psychiatry. 2026;69(S1):S523-S524. doi:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.11149.
